skill.description: Model agent beliefs, desires, intentions, plans, and reasoning traces with BDI ontology patterns, RDF transformations, and SPARQL validation.
skill.summary: Build explainable BDI mental-state models grounded in RDF world states.
skill.author: muratcankoylan

security_audit.summary: All 130 static findings are false positives caused by RDF identifiers, Markdown backticks, and BDI terminology. No static item performs network access, command execution, scheduling, or reconnaissance. One medium-risk prompt-injection weakness exists in the documented LAG implementation.

remediation.issue: The LAG example places untrusted context and parser errors directly inside model prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Use separate trusted instructions, delimit untrusted data, reject instruction-like content, and validate generated RDF against allowed entities and actions.

content.user_title: Model Agent Mental States with BDI
content.value_statement: Agent decisions become difficult to explain when beliefs, goals, and commitments lack formal structure. This skill models BDI chains with RDF, SPARQL, provenance, and temporal validity.
actual_capabilities: Models beliefs, desires, intentions, plans, tasks, and world states with formal BDI relationships.
Transforms external RDF context into grounded belief chains and projects action results back into RDF.
Adds justifications, provenance links, and temporal validity to mental states.
Provides Turtle patterns for cognitive chains, planning, composition, and multi-agent coordination.
Provides SPARQL competency queries for motivation, provenance, planning, time, and validation.
Maps BDI ontology concepts to SEMAS, JADE, JADEX, triple stores, and FIPA ACL.
limitations: Provides modeling guidance and examples but does not execute an ontology reasoner or agent runtime.
Example namespaces, classes, and framework adapters require adaptation to each project.
Structural validation does not guarantee that generated beliefs or intentions are factually correct.
LLM integrations require additional prompt-injection controls for untrusted context.

use_cases.title: Design a Semantic Agent Model
use_cases.description: Define BDI classes and relations that connect perceived world states to explainable decisions.

use_cases.title: Trace Agent Decisions
use_cases.description: Create belief-to-desire-to-intention chains with plans, justifications, and validity intervals.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Cognitive Representations
use_cases.description: Use competency questions to test provenance, motivation, plan order, and temporal consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Identify BDI Elements
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify the beliefs, desires, intentions, world states, and plans in this scenario: [scenario]. Explain each classification.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cognitive Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Model [scenario] as a grounded belief-to-desire-to-intention chain. Include a plan, justification, and temporal validity for each mental state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a complete explainable decision chain.

prompt_templates.title: Design Competency Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft SPARQL competency questions for this BDI model: [model description]. Cover provenance, motivation, plan order, validity, and world-state grounding.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare validation criteria for an ontology.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Framework Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a BDI integration for [framework and system]. Specify RDF transformations, validation gates, storage, communication, and prompt-injection controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt the model to a production agent architecture.

output_examples.input: Model an agent that learns an invoice is due and commits to paying it.
output: World state: The invoice is due tomorrow.
Belief: The agent accepts the due date based on billing-system evidence.
Intention: Pay the invoice using the approved payment plan.

output_examples.input: Explain how to validate a time-sensitive belief model.
output_examples.output: Check that each belief references a world state, includes justification, has a validity interval, and does not conflict with overlapping beliefs.

output_examples.input: Choose between BDI modeling and ordinary persistent memory.
output_examples.output: Use BDI when the system must explain motivations, commitments, and plans. Use persistent memory when it only needs retained facts.

best_practices: Ground every belief in a distinct world state and explicit evidence.
Give mental states validity intervals and test overlapping claims.
Validate motivation, commitment, plan order, and provenance with competency queries.
anti_patterns: Do not treat world states and agent beliefs as the same entity.
Do not commit an intention without a motivating desire and specified plan.
Do not accept LLM-generated RDF based only on syntax validation.

faq.question: What does BDI mean?
faq.answer: BDI means belief, desire, and intention. It models what an agent accepts, wants, and commits to doing.

faq.question: Does this skill execute agent plans?
faq.answer: No. It provides ontology, transformation, query, and integration patterns for systems that execute plans.

faq.question: Which data formats does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes RDF and Turtle for representation, plus SPARQL for querying and validation.

faq.question: Can it support multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes shared mental-state queries and FIPA ACL mapping patterns for agent communication.

faq.question: How does it improve explainability?
faq.answer: It links beliefs to evidence, desires to motivations, intentions to plans, and actions to resulting world states.

faq.question: Is generated RDF automatically trustworthy?
faq.answer: No. Validate syntax, ontology constraints, factual grounding, allowed entities, and resistance to prompt injection before use.
